_comment: The world in 1926. pos is [column, row] on the ASCII map in ui/art/map.txt. Routes go both ways.

locations.name: Yukon Wilds
locations.text: Gold-rush ghost towns sink into the snow. Trappers no longer come back from the high passes.

locations.name: Los Angeles
locations.text: Orange groves, oil derricks, and a film studio that shoots only at night.

locations.name: Chicago
locations.text: Bootleggers run the streets. Someone else runs the bootleggers.

locations.name: New York
locations.text: Seven million people, and not one of them looks up at the new star over the harbor.

locations.name: Providence
locations.text: Old colonial houses lean over narrow hills. The university library keeps some books in a locked cellar.

locations.name: New Orleans
locations.text: Jazz in the Quarter, and drums in the bayou that answer it.

locations.name: Mexico City
locations.text: A modern capital built on the drowned temples of an older one.

locations.name: Yucatan Jungle
locations.text: Limestone wells drop into black water. The ruins here are older than the people who claim them.

locations.name: Caribbean Sea
locations.text: Warm, bright water. Ships still vanish in it.

locations.name: Nazca Desert
locations.text: Lines in the desert floor, drawn for something that sees only from very high up.

locations.name: Mato Grosso
locations.text: An explorer went in last year to find a lost city. His last letter says he found it.

locations.name: Rio de Janeiro
locations.text: Mountains rise straight out of the bay. Carnival masks hang in shop windows all year.

locations.name: Tierra del Fuego
locations.text: The end of the world, where the wind never stops and the fires on the hills are not always made by men.

locations.name: North Atlantic
locations.text: Grey swells and icebergs. Radio operators hear voices between the stations.

locations.name: South Atlantic
locations.text: Long empty miles of ocean under a sky with too many stars.

locations.name: Reykjavik
locations.text: A small harbor town at the edge of the Arctic. The old sagas mention things that walk on the glacier.

locations.name: Paris
locations.text: Cafes, salons, and occult societies that meet in the catacombs below.

locations.name: Prague
locations.text: Alchemists once worked in the castle lanes. Some of their furnaces are still warm.

locations.name: Moscow
locations.text: A new government, old churches, and secret police who ask about your dreams.

locations.name: Siberian Taiga
locations.text: Endless forest. Some years ago a fire fell from the sky here and flattened it for miles.

locations.name: Athens
locations.text: White ruins over a busy port. The oracles are long dead, but people still have visions.

locations.name: Marrakesh
locations.text: Storytellers in the great square tell one tale that no one may finish.

locations.name: The Sahara
locations.text: Dunes move at night. Caravans find stone cities, and cannot find them again.

locations.name: Cairo
locations.text: Dig sites, museums, and a black market in things that should stay buried.

locations.name: Congo Basin
locations.text: River and rainforest. The villages here warn you not to follow the singing.

locations.name: Cape Town
locations.text: A busy port under a flat mountain. Sailors say the cloud on it is not always cloud.

locations.name: Baghdad
locations.text: Booksellers on Al-Mutanabbi Street trade in copies of copies of books that were burned.

locations.name: Empty Quarter
locations.text: Sand without end. Bedouin guides speak of a nameless city with doors too low for men.

locations.name: Indian Ocean
locations.text: Monsoon winds and trade routes older than any empire.

locations.name: Bombay
locations.text: Mills, markets, and temples. A thousand languages, and some of them are not human.

locations.name: Tibetan Plateau
locations.text: Monasteries cling to cliffs. The monks keep watch over a door in the mountain.

locations.name: Gobi Desert
locations.text: Dinosaur bones and older things lie just under the stones.

locations.name: Peking
locations.text: Warlords fight over the old capital. In the Forbidden City, the clocks all stopped at the same hour.

locations.name: Hong Kong
locations.text: Junks and steamers crowd the harbor. Opium dens deal in a darker smoke.

locations.name: Singapore
locations.text: The crossroads of the East. Every ship stops here, and so does everything on the ships.

locations.name: Yokohama
locations.text: Rebuilt after the great earthquake. Fishermen say the quake came from below the sea, not below the land.

locations.name: North Pacific
locations.text: The widest stretch of water on Earth. Something under it is very large and very patient.

locations.name: South Pacific
locations.text: The point farthest from any land. Sailors who pass it dream of a green stone city.

locations.name: Great Sandy Desert
locations.text: Red sand and ancient blocks of stone that no one placed there.

locations.name: Melbourne
locations.text: A proud southern city. Its university keeps a collection of stones that whisper.
